findings.where: First screen, the action row: the filled blue 'Write to me' button and the underlined address 'Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com' beside it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page's one main action does nothing. 'Write to me' looks like a filled button, and the address is underlined in the way a link is, but both are static: neither is a link or a button. The motion table even gives them hover states ('Button blue to ink; address underline to ink'). The only working mailto is in the footer, at the very bottom of the page.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who decides to contact Mark from the hero clicks 'Write to me' or the address and nothing happens. The brief's whole first screen exists to get this contact, so the visitor ends up copying the address by hand or gives up.

findings.where: First screen, the action row: 'Book a consultation' (link to #consult)
findings.fault: The link goes to #consult, but the page has no consultation section or booking form, so it is a dead action. It also promises a booking service that a brochure site with no bespoke software (sheet §6) does not offer.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks it expecting a calendar or booking form gets nowhere, or the page jumps. It costs trust on the step most likely to lead to an engagement.

findings.where: First screen, the action row: 'Write to me' and 'Book a consultation' side by side
findings.fault: There are two filled blue buttons of equal weight, so the page has no single main action. The brief asks for one direct, personal way to reach Mark and one action on the first screen, and the visitor has to work out which of the two to use and how they differ.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose test asks for one personal way to reach Mark. A visitor also hesitates between 'write' and 'book' when both mean contacting the same man.

findings.where: First screen, left margin notes ('Istanbul, 2025 / Best Practices in PPP Legislation…', 'Melbourne, 2026 / LLM Course on PPP Law…', 'São Paulo, 2024 / New Approaches to Risk Allocation…'); also the blue section labels below the fold (Palette, Type, Texture, Article page, Motion, Tile notes)
findings.fault: The notes are set in the link blue, the colour the palette reserves for 'links, the action', and they name talks by title, so they read as links to those talks. All of them are static. The brief asks for blue margin notes, so this is a clash between that rule and the link colour's meaning, and it goes to the founder.
findings.who_objects: A visitor curious about the Istanbul or São Paulo talk clicks the blue title expecting the slides or the article and nothing happens. They then trust the blue less where it really is a link.
